matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, recompute the integer values of both sides of the equation and verify that they are equal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a candidate transformed equation is produced, always evaluate both sides numerically before finalising the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation without confirming that the left‑hand and right‑hand values actually match.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting glyph must correspond to a valid Roman‑numeral symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After the stick move, check each altered numeral against the list of allowed Roman symbols (I, V, X, L, C, D, M).
matchstick.example: Creating a shape consisting of a single diagonal stick, which does not represent any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only relocate it preserving that orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When selecting a stick to move, ensure the destination position uses the same orientation as the source.
matchstick.example: Rotating a vertical stick into a diagonal position to form a new numeral.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect at most the source character (which loses one stick) and the destination character (which gains one stick).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After moving a stick, verify that only the two involved characters have changed; no other symbols should be altered.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one numeral and unintentionally altering a third character as a side‑effect.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The equality sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; you cannot remove, add, or alter it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Treat ‘=’ as immutable throughout the puzzle; never use it as a source or destination for a stick.
matchstick.example: Removing one of the horizontal bars of ‘=’ or turning it into ‘≠’.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Use known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both characters valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral’s value needs to be adjusted, look for a standard single‑stick transformation that yields another valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn I directly into V, which requires more than one stick change.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final output must be a single line starting with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the corrected equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have the correct equation, output exactly one line with that prefix and no extra whitespace or lines.
matchstick.example: Providing multiple lines or omitting the required prefix, causing the answer to be unparsable.

matchstick.title: Plus-to-minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If the equation contains a ‘+’, you may move its vertical stick to another character, turning ‘+’ into ‘-’ while adjusting the other character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic difference suggests that a subtraction could balance the equation, consider converting ‘+’ to ‘-’ by relocating its vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ but forgetting to place it elsewhere, leaving the operator as ‘-’ without a valid destination.

matchstick.title: 5‑unit diagonal swap
matchstick.principle: When the absolute difference between the two sides is exactly 5 (or a multiple thereof), try moving a diagonal stick to change an X to V (or vice‑versa) and adjust the value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation is off by 5, consider a diagonal move that changes a numeral’s value by 5 (e.g., X→V).
matchstick.example: Ignoring a 5‑unit discrepancy and not attempting a diagonal move, missing the X→V transformation.

matchstick.title: Within‑character diagonal repositioning
matchstick.principle: You may relocate a diagonal stick within the same numeral (source and destination are the same character) to change its shape, e.g., reposition a diagonal in X to turn it into V, adjusting its value by 5 while keeping the character valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the puzzle includes an X (or V) and the needed value change is 5, consider moving one of its diagonal sticks to a new position inside that character rather than between characters.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change X to V by moving a diagonal to another character, leaving X invalid; the correct move is to reposition the diagonal within X itself.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual stick move and forgets to check whether the resulting equation actually balances.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the numeric values of both sides after any transformation and confirm equality before finalising the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks without considering the set of allowed Roman‑numeral glyphs, producing shapes that do not correspond to any numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each stick move, verify that every altered character matches a known Roman numeral; discard moves that yield unknown shapes.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When relocating sticks involving ‘+’ or ‘-’, the model may produce an operator that no longer matches the allowed symbols.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat operators as fixed patterns (‘+’ = vertical + horizontal, ‘-’ = single horizontal); ensure any stick removal or addition leaves a valid operator.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick from a source character but fails to place it on a valid destination, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Every stick that is taken from a source must be explicitly placed on a destination character; double‑check that the destination is specified and valid.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Changing a ‘+’ to ‘-’ (or vice‑versa) without adjusting the surrounding expression can leave the equation syntactically incorrect.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When converting ‘+’ to ‘-’, ensure the rest of the expression still makes sense (e.g., the right‑hand side remains a valid arithmetic term).
